question: Widen the six-return affine clock box and bound independent timing, readout and preparation errors.

objects.definition: Six scalar R exp(((1+gamma)*t+Delta)*A_g(theta)) S diagonal port returns
objects.basis_orientation: PR #120 signed simplex order and prior rational K basis

assumptions: Fixed Q167/Q173-style masks with candidate weighted adjoints
One common affine time warp across all samples

technique_plan.technique: Exact rational Taylor and operator norm bounds

technique_plan.purpose_or_na_reason: Continuous affine time and no divisibility question

dynamics_readout.initial_boundary_conditions: Embedded unit coarse port; fixed mask for each return

target_exposure.status: Design scan only; no empirical data
target_exposure.selection_criterion: Minimum numerical inverse infinity norm among scan choices

calculation_steps: Reuse the rational baseline Jacobian and tail from affine-001.
Bound H-induced norms by weighted Frobenius trace; baseline sum caps are 58 for H^-1 K and 27 for DG.
Transport by metric equivalence to get caps 59 and 28 throughout the box, then bound Hessian below 9200.
Enclose each time slope using the baseline Taylor series, a mixed derivative bound and the second time derivative bound 64.

result.exact_expression: Inverse Lipschitz <=420 on radius 1/4000000; each return budget epsilon_i+L_i |jitter_i|+p_i <=1/6720000000.
result.precision_and_error: Slope caps in schedule order: 1/10, 7/200, 39/1000, 53/1000, 1733/1000, 4/5; jitter window 1/100000; p_i is true metric norm error or twice fine Euclidean error. Two compatible fits separate by <=840 max channel budget.
result.scope: Candidate model and declared box only

verification.method: exact rational assertions and numeric design scan

counterexamples_and_failures: At five samples and a locally invertible metric-plus-offset sub-Jacobian, rate changes can be compensated locally by those five coordinates.
limitations: No native actuator, independent timing jitter model or physical time conversion; no independent review.
next_discriminant: Search a better-conditioned schedule subject to timing sensitivity and test the noise contract against a specified readout.
